approachQuestion.prompt: A lowercase message s must be split into nonempty words from a given list. A listed word may be reused any number of times. Return whether the whole message can be split. Examples: s="redblue", words=["red","blue"] → true; s="aaaa", words=["aa"] → true; s="abc", words=["ab","bc"] → false. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 1 ≤ n=s.length ≤ 2000; 1 ≤ k=words.length ≤ 100; each distinct word has length 1 through L, where L is the maximum listed length and L ≤ 30. Input strings are read-only. Return a Boolean.

options.text: Keep reachable prefix endpoints, starting with endpoint zero. For each endpoint i from 1 through n, test every listed word whose length is at most i. If its start endpoint is reachable and its characters match s ending at i, mark i reachable. Compare characters directly by index.
options.feedback: A reachable prefix and an exactly matching final word describe a valid split. Every valid split has such a final word, so considering all words is exhaustive.

options.text: Use the same endpoint tests, but store a k-entry Boolean row per endpoint indicating whether each possible final word completes a reachable prefix. Derive reachability by OR-ing the row, and retain every row.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: At the current position choose the longest matching word and never reconsider it.
options.feedback: For s="abcd", words=["abc","ab","cd"], choosing abc gets stuck, but ab followed by cd succeeds.

options.text: Return true if every character of s occurs somewhere in at least one listed word.
options.feedback: For s="ba", words=["ab"], both letters occur but no legal split exists.

feedback.reason: Represent all feasible split endpoints instead of committing to a greedy final word.
details: Allocate n+1 Boolean prefix entries. For each i=1..n scan all k words, checking length, reachable start, and then characters directly until mismatch or full match. Keep scanning words even after i becomes reachable. Store no substrings and no word-matching table.

A valid split of prefix i ends with some listed word whose preceding prefix is reachable. Compare characters directly to avoid substring allocations. The specified implementation still tests later dictionary words after finding a match.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Allocate n+1 Boolean prefix entries. For each i=1..n scan all k words, checking length, reachable start, and then characters directly until mismatch or full match. Keep scanning words even after i becomes reachable. Store no substrings and no word-matching table. Analyze this fixed implementation. N=n; n,k,L vary as parameters within the bounds; analyze worst-case families with n at least 2L. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: Account for every prefix, dictionary word, and possible character comparison.
details: At most n·k comparisons each inspect up to L characters; repetitive strings and overlapping words attain the product. Prefix flags occupy n+1 words. Dictionary strings are input, and no hashes, copies, tries, or call stack are used.
“O(nk) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A tested word may require L character comparisons; comparisons are not constant-time string lookups.
“O(nkL) time, O(nk) auxiliary space”: The endpoint method retains one reachable flag per prefix, not one flag per prefix and final word.
“O(nkL) time, O(nL) auxiliary space”: Word characters are compared directly from read-only input. No prefix-by-word-length workspace is allocated.
